title: Ordinary adic adjunction over an arbitrary field
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $\ell$ be a prime invertible in $k$, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-morphism between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use $\mathcal C_T=D^b_c(T,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], with the completed pullback $Lf^*$ of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] and the derived direct image $Rf_*$ of [def-weil-derived-direct-image], rationalized and passed to common finite coefficient-field stages. These operations restrict to exact triangulated functors $Lf^*:\mathcal C_Y\to\mathcal C_X$ and $Rf_*:\mathcal C_X\to\mathcal C_Y$, and there is a natural adjunction
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_X}(Lf^*A,B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_Y}(A,Rf_*B).$$
The adjunction is compatible with shifts and finite coefficient-field extension.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.2 (including its adjunction), Proposition 6.8.14 and Remark 6.8.15

proof.text: A field is Noetherian. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to $X,Y$ over $\operatorname{Spec}k$, and [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] to obtain Noetherian finite-dimensional schemes. Invertibility of $\ell$ pulls back from $k$. Thus both schemes satisfy the hypotheses of the raw finite-stage categories and the scalar-extension comparisons [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. The separated finite-type $k$-morphism in the item satisfies the morphism hypothesis of [lem-a1-rational-direct-image-realization], which in fact allows any $k$-morphism between these separated finite-type schemes.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.2, Proposition 6.8.14(1),(2), Remark 6.8.15; explicit pair-category passage

proof.text: At each finite field $E$ write $\mathcal C_E(W)=D^b_c(W,E)$ using [def-weil-pbc-rational-category], $P_E=Lf^*_{\mathrm{comp},E}$ and $D_E=Rf_{*,E}$. The completed pullback is precisely [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]; only the finite and integral constructions of [def-weil-derived-direct-image] are used to define $D_E$, followed by raw rationalization. By [lem-a1-rational-direct-image-realization] these functors preserve the bounded constructible categories and have the canonical adjunction $h_E$. The equivalence $J$ of [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization] identifies this with the ambient continuous-module adjunction, including its actual unit and counit. Exactness requires no change of triangulation: [lem-cbc-completed-pullback-triangles] gives the shift and triangle comparisons of the specified integral completed pullback, and [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated] gives them for the ordinary ringed-topos direct image identified with the strict-tower operation by the realization statement. The coefficient integers are Noetherian DVRs by [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], so the quotients used for the completed pullback are perfect, with the two-term resolution given by multiplication by $\varpi^n$. Both integral functors are coefficient-linear: their complex and strict-tower maps preserve the constant coefficient action, so applying either construction to $c u$ gives $c$ times its value on $u$; the same equality holds on derived morphisms. Their raw rationalizations are exact by [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport].

proof.text:
For $E\subset L$, abbreviate the specified comparisons of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] by $a_{L/E}:T_XP_E\to P_LT_Y$ and $b_{L/E}:T_YD_E\to D_LT_X$. Apply [lem-per-arbitrary-field-adjunction-scalars] to this arbitrary field $k$, the given morphism, and these raw rationalized stages. Its mate equation gives, for $u:P_EA\to B$,
$$h_L(T_X(u)a_A^{-1})=b_B T_Y(h_E(u)).$$
It gives the inverse equation as well, for these exact $a,b$, and identity, tower and shift compatibility. This is the needed scalar-naturality input; compatibility of a direct-image realization alone would not imply this equation. No finite-field datum or Karoubi coefficient category is used.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.2, Proposition 6.8.14(1),(2), Remark 6.8.15; explicit pair-category passage

proof.text:
Construct functors directly on the pair category of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category, def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category]. On objects put $P(E,A)=(E,P_EA)$ and $D(E,B)=(E,D_EB)$. For $F=P$ or $D$ write $c^P=a$, $c^D=b$. If $[M,u]:(E,K)\to(E',K')$, define
$$F[M,u]=[M,(c^F_{M/E',K'})^{-1}F_M(u)c^F_{M/E,K}].$$
The map inside brackets goes from $T_{M/E}F_EK$ to $T_{M/E'}F_{E'}K'$, so has the required pair-category type. For an extension $M\subset N$, the tower equation for $c^F$ in [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension], followed by naturality, identifies this formula at $N$ with the associator-conjugate extension of the formula at $M$. Hence eventually equal representatives have eventually equal images. The unit comparison makes identities map to identities. At a common stage the middle $c^F(c^F)^{-1}$ cancels in a composite, proving composition; additivity follows there too. These formulas define the completed pullback and rationalized direct image on this pair category, using their given finite-stage operations.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.2, Proposition 6.8.14(1),(2), Remark 6.8.15; explicit pair-category passage

proof.text:
Let $A=(E,A_E)$ and $B=(F,B_F)$. An arrow $P A\to B$ is represented by $u:T_{M/E}P_EA_E\to T_{M/F}B_F$. Define
$$\Psi[M,u]=[M,b_{M/F,B_F}^{-1}\,h_M(u\,a_{M/E,A_E}^{-1})].$$
Here $u a^{-1}$ has source $P_MT_{M/E}A_E$, and the displayed adjunct has target $T_{M/F}D_FB_F$, as required for an arrow $A\to D B$. Conversely define
$$\Phi[M,v]=[M,h_M^{-1}(b_{M/F,B_F}v)\,a_{M/E,A_E}].$$
For $M\subset N$, use the scalar equation of Step 3 with input $u a^{-1}$ and then the tower equations for $a,b$. This gives $\Psi_N(u_N)=(\Psi_M(u))_N$, with both transports precisely the associator conjugations in [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category]. The inverse scalar equation gives the same identity for $\Phi$. Thus both formulas respect eventual equality and define maps on the pair Hom sets. At one stage, $h_M^{-1}h_M=1$ and $h_Mh_M^{-1}=1$, and the neighboring $a,a^{-1}$ and $b,b^{-1}$ cancel. Consequently $\Phi\Psi=1$ and $\Psi\Phi=1$.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.2, Proposition 6.8.14(1),(2), Remark 6.8.15; explicit pair-category passage

proof.text: Naturality is checked at one common finite stage. Substitute the formula of Step 4 for a map in either variable into Step 5. Naturality of $a,b$ moves these comparisons through the maps, and naturality of the finite-stage bijection $h_M$ identifies precomposition by $P$ of a map with precomposition by that map, and postcomposition with postcomposition by $D$ of that map. The inverse comparisons cancel, yielding the two pair-category naturality equations. The finite-stage naturality is supplied by [lem-a1-rational-direct-image-realization]. By the shift clause of [lem-per-arbitrary-field-adjunction-scalars], shifting $u$ and inserting the operation shift comparisons in the formula for $\Psi$ gives the shifted formula for $\Psi(u)$. The scalar shift comparisons commute with $a,b$ by [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension], so this calculation also holds for pairs represented at different fields and for all integer shifts.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.2, Proposition 6.8.14(1),(2), Remark 6.8.15; explicit pair-category passage

proof.text: It remains to verify exactness with the actual common-stage cones [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones]. Let $[M,u]:(E,K)\to(F,L)$ and choose its stage-$M$ distinguished triangle $T_{M/E}K\to T_{M/F}L\to C(u)\to(T_{M/E}K)[1]$. For $F=P$ or $D$, apply the exact finite-stage functor $F_M$ from Step 2. The resulting distinguished triangle defines a distinguished common-stage triangle. The image under the pair functor of the original common-stage cone triangle is isomorphic to this triangle: on the first two vertices the isomorphisms are $c^F_{M/E,K}$ and $c^F_{M/F,L}$, and on the cone vertex it is the identity on $F_M C(u)$. On arrows this follows by the conjugation formula of Step 4. On the closing arrow, the definition uses $\sigma_{M/E,K}^{-1}p_u$; the shift compatibility of $c^F$ in [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] identifies its image with the closing arrow of the $F_M$-image triangle. The same operation shift comparisons define the pair functor's commutation with shift. Since every distinguished pair triangle is isomorphic to such a cone triangle, both pair functors are exact triangulated.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.2, Proposition 6.8.14(1),(2), Remark 6.8.15; explicit pair-category passage

proof.text: For a representative already over $E$, the formulas of Steps 4 and 5 reduce to $P_E,D_E,h_E$ by the identity comparisons. Moving it to a further finite field $L$ changes its adjunct by exactly $h_L(T_Xu\,a^{-1})=b\,T_Yh_E(u)$ of [lem-per-arbitrary-field-adjunction-scalars]. Thus the constructed adjunction is compatible with every finite coefficient extension, with the prescribed units and counits: they are the adjuncts of the identity arrows, so the same equation applies to them. Tower compatibility gives the same result after successive extensions. With Steps 6 and 7 this proves all clauses of the unchanged statement on $\mathcal C_X,\mathcal C_Y$.
